guidance: Follow SD Internal Guidance Note Hub process Nutrient Neutrality_April update FINAL.pdf or Hub Guidance for agricultural developments.pdf (for agricultural developments). If consultation includes HRA/AA or is a standalone mitigation scheme, refer to Central Casework Team.
response_paragraph:
Further information required - potential water quality/nutrient impacts to European Sites (habitats sites)  
This development site is within the catchment of a European Site (habitats site) vulnerable to nutrient impacts. 
Within this location, proposals with the potential to affect water quality may have a likely significant effect on the qualifying features of the European Site (habitats site) through adverse nutrient impacts.
Natural England advises that such developments require a Habitats Regulations Assessment (HRA), which has been informed by nutrient budget calculations (Using the nutrient neutrality calculators - GOV.UK (www.gov.uk) or local calculator if preferred), to consider the impacts, alone and in combination with other plans/projects, proceeding to appropriate assessment stage where likely significant effects cannot be ruled out. 
The HRA should take into consideration the Natural England Access to Evidence - Conservation Objectives for European Sites and it will need to set out in detail any mitigation measures that will be secured in this case, along with the necessary justification of their likely efficacy to ensure there is no adverse effect on the integrity of the site in accordance with the Conservation of Habitats and Species Regulations 2017 (as amended). 
Natural England must be consulted on any proposals which reach the appropriate assessment stage of HRA. With the consultation, please include a nutrient mitigation strategy including information on the management and monitoring of the proposed mitigation measures along with details of how they will be secured and funded in perpetuity.
Please refer to Strategic Solutions: Nutrient Neutrality (naturalengland.org.uk) for further information. 
Please be aware that if the information requested is not supplied, Natural England may need to consider objecting to the proposal based on potential harm to the habitats site(s).

guidance: Send this paragraph for all development proposals including householders where no Hydrology Report included. If Hydrology Report included refer to Central Casework Team.
response_paragraph:
Further information required - potential water quality/supply impacts to Burnham Beeches Special Area of Conservation (SAC) 
This development site is within the groundwater and surface water catchment of Burnham Beeches Special Area of Conservation (SAC), a European site afforded protection under The Conservation of Habitats and Species Regulations 2017 (as amended). The site is also notified at a national level as National Nature Reserve (NNR) and a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI).
Within this location, development proposals may have a likely significant effect on the qualifying features of the SAC by adversely affecting the quality and quantity of water reaching the site. 
Natural England advises that all developments proposals require:
A Hydrology Report to assess the impacts of the development on the catchment that flows into Burnham Beeches SAC, and
A sustainable urban drainage system (SUDS) of sufficient capacity (including an allowance for climate change predictions) to maintain the quality and quantity of water reaching the Burnham Beeches.    
Please consult Natural England once your authority has received this information. 
Please refer to Development Management Guidance Note: Hydrology in Burnham Beeches (February 2014) for further information. 
Please be aware that if the information requested is not supplied, Natural England may need to consider objecting to the proposal based on potential harm to Burnham Beeches SAC.

This development site is within the zone of influence (ZoI) for air quality impacts to Epping Forest Special Area of Conservation (EFSAC).  
Within this ZoI, proposals for any net increase in Annual Average Daily Traffic (AADT) on roads within the EFSAC or on roads within 200m of the EFSAC may have a likely significant effect on the qualifying features of the SAC through impacts on air quality. 
Natural England advises that such developments require a Habitats Regulations Assessment (HRA) to consider the impacts, alone and in combination with other plans/projects, proceeding to appropriate assessment stage where likely significant effects cannot be ruled out. Please see Epping Forest District Council’s EFSAC Guidance for applicants for assessing air quality impacts.
The HRA should take into consideration the Natural England Access to Evidence - Conservation Objectives for European Sites and it will need to set out in detail any mitigation measures that will be secured in this case, along with the necessary justification of their likely efficacy to ensure there is no adverse effect on the integrity of the site(s) in accordance with the Conservation of Habitats and Species Regulations 2017 (as amended).

guidance: Send this paragraph for any net increase in residential units where no Habitats Regulations Assessment (HRA) included. If HRA included refer to Central Casework Team.
response_paragraph:
Further information required - recreational pressure impacts to European Sites (habitats sites) 
This development site is within the zone of influence (ZoI) for recreational pressure impacts to one or more European Sites (habitats sites).
Within this ZoI, proposals for any net increase in residential units will have a likely significant effect on the qualifying features of the European Site(s) (habitats site(s)) through increased recreational pressure when considered either alone or in combination with other plans and projects. 
Your authority has measures in place to manage these potential impacts through a strategic solution which Natural England considers will be effective in preventing adverse impacts on the integrity of the site(s).  
Notwithstanding this, Natural England advises that these measures should be formally checked and confirmed by your authority, as the competent authority, via an appropriate assessment in view of the Natural England Access to Evidence - Conservation Objectives for European Sites and in accordance with the Conservation of Habitats & Species Regulations 2017 (as amended). 
Providing the appropriate assessment concludes that the measures can be secured, it is likely that Natural England will be satisfied that there will be no adverse effect on the integrity of the European Site(s) (habitats site(s)) in relation to recreational disturbance.
Where the proposal includes bespoke mitigation that falls outside of the strategic solution, Natural England should be consulted. 
Reserved Matters applications, and in some cases the discharge/removal/variation of conditions, where the permission was granted prior to the introduction of the strategic approach, should also be subject to the requirements of the Conservation of Habitats & Species Regulations 2017 (as amended) and our advice above applies

response_paragraph:
Further information required - potential recreational impacts to The New Forest Special Area of Conservation (SAC), Special Protection Area (SPA) and Ramsar site
This development site is within the 13.8km zone of influence (ZoI) for recreational impacts to The New Forest Special Area of Conservation (SAC), Special Protection Area (SPA) and Ramsar site.
Research into recreational use of the New Forest’s protected habitats - New Forest National Park Authority (newforestnpa.gov.uk) (opens in a new tab) shows that within 13.8km of The New Forest SAC, SPA and Ramsar site, proposals for any net increase in residential units may have a likely significant effect on the site’s qualifying features though increased recreational impacts (including disturbance, trampling, eutrophication amongst others). 
Natural England advises that such developments require a Habitats Regulations Assessment (HRA) to consider the impacts, alone and in combination with other plans/projects, proceeding to appropriate assessment stage where likely significant effects cannot be ruled out. 
The HRA should take into consideration the Natural England Access to Evidence - Conservation Objectives for European Sites and it will need to set out in detail any mitigation measures that will be secured in this case, along with the necessary justification of their likely efficacy to ensure there is no adverse effect on the integrity of the site in accordance with the Conservation of Habitats and Species Regulations 2017 (as amended).

The HRA should take into consideration the Natural England Access to Evidence - Conservation Objectives for European Sites and it will need to set out in detail any mitigation measures that will be secured in this case, along with the necessary justification of their likely efficacy to ensure there is no adverse effect on the integrity of the site(s) in accordance with the Conservation of Habitats and Species Regulations 2017 (as amended).  
Natural England must be consulted on any proposals which reach the appropriate assessment stage of HRA. 
Proposals for residential developments of fewer than 50 units in this location are unlikely to have a significant effect on the qualifying features of the SAC through increased recreational pressure.

guidance: Send this paragraph for any net increase in residential units or visitor accommodation where no Habitats Regulations Assessment (HRA) included. If HRA included refer to area team
response_paragraph:
Further information required - recreational pressure impacts to European Sites (habitats sites) 
This development site is within the zone of influence (ZoI) for recreational pressure impacts to one or more European Sites (habitats sites).
Within this ZoI, proposals for any net increase in residential units or visitor accommodation will have a likely significant effect on the qualifying features of the European Site(s) (habitats site(s)) through increased recreational pressure when considered either alone or in combination with other plans and projects.
Your authority has measures in place to manage these potential impacts through a strategic solution which Natural England considers will be effective in preventing adverse impacts on the integrity of the site(s).  
Notwithstanding this, Natural England advises that these measures should be formally checked and confirmed by your authority, as the competent authority, via an appropriate assessment in view of the Natural England Access to Evidence - Conservation Objectives for European Sites and in accordance with the Conservation of Habitats & Species Regulations 2017 (as amended).
Providing the appropriate assessment concludes that the measures can be secured, it is likely that Natural England will be satisfied that there will be no adverse effect on the integrity of the European Site(s) (habitats site(s)) in relation to recreational disturbance.
Where the proposal includes bespoke mitigation that falls outside of the strategic solution, Natural England should be consulted. 
Reserved Matters applications, and in some cases the discharge/removal/variation of conditions, where the permission was granted prior to the introduction of the strategic approach, should also be subject to the requirements of the Conservation of Habitats & Species Regulations 2017 (as amended) and our advice above applies.

The HRA should take into consideration the Natural England Access to Evidence - Conservation Objectives for European Sites and it will need to set out in detail any mitigation measures that will be secured in this case, along with the necessary justification of their likely efficacy to ensure there is no adverse effect on the integrity of the site in accordance with the Conservation of Habitats and Species Regulations 2017 (as amended). 
Natural England must be consulted on any proposals which reach the appropriate assessment stage of HRA.
Proposals for residential developments or tourist accommodation of fewer than 500 units in this location are considered unlikely to have a significant effect on the qualifying features of the SAC, through increased recreational pressure.

guidance: Send this paragraph for all developments where no Habitats Regulations Assessment (HRA) included. If Appropriate Assessment (AA) included refer to area team.
response_paragraph:
Further information required - potential impacts to Humber Estuary Special Protection Area (SPA) and Ramsar site
This development site is within the South Humber Bank mitigation zone. 
Within this ZoI, development proposals on greenfield land will have a likely significant effect on the qualifying features of Humber Estuary Special Protection Area (SPA) and Ramsar site through loss of supporting habitat when considered either alone or in combination with other plans and projects.  Exceptionally, brownfield sites may have a likely significant effect if evidence identifies that SPA/Ramsar birds have been using the site in significant numbers. 
Your authority has measures in place to manage these potential impacts through a strategic approach which Natural England considers will be effective in preventing adverse impacts on the integrity of the site.  
Notwithstanding this, Natural England advises that these measures should be formally checked and confirmed by your authority, as the competent authority, via a Habitats Regulations Assessment in view of Natural England Access to Evidence - Conservation Objectives for European Sites and in accordance with the Conservation of Habitats & Species Regulations 2017 (as amended). Your authority should determine whether the proposal is likely to have a significant effect on any European site, proceeding to the Appropriate Assessment stage where significant effects cannot be ruled out. 
Natural England must be consulted on the appropriate assessment.  
Where the proposal includes bespoke mitigation that falls outside of the strategic solution, Natural England should be consulted. 
Reserved Matters applications, and in some cases the discharge/removal/variation of conditions, where the permission was granted prior to the introduction of the strategic approach, should also be subject to the requirements of the Conservation of Habitats & Species Regulations 2017 (as amended) and our advice above applies. 
Please refer to Policy 9 of  2018 - New Local Plan 2013 to 2032 (nelincs.gov.uk) for further information.

response_paragraph:
Further information required - potential impacts to Eversden and Wimpole Woods Special Area of Conservation (SAC)
This development site is within the core sustenance zone (CSZ) for Eversden and Wimpole Woods Special Area of Conservation (SAC). 
Within the CSZ, proposals which could increase lighting levels, restrict the movement of commuting bats at a local or landscape scale, affect potential roosting features such as trees, rural buildings/structures (manmade or natural), or impact barbastelle foraging resources such as waterbodies, streams and rivers, riparian habitats, damp grassland, golf courses, hedgerows, orchards and woodland, may have a likely significant effect on Eversden and Wimpole Woods SAC. 
Natural England advises that all planning applications (except householder applications) where the proposed development is outside or extends outside existing settlements/urban areas and where any of the above applies will require a Habitats Regulations Assessment (HRA) to consider the impacts, alone and in combination with other plans/projects, (for both construction and operation phases) proceeding to appropriate assessment stage where likely significant effects cannot be ruled out. 
The HRA should take into consideration the Natural England Access to Evidence - Conservation Objectives for European Sites and Supplementary Advice on Conservation Objectives available via Designated Sites View. It will need to set out in detail any mitigation measures that will be secured in this case, along with the necessary justification of their likely efficacy to ensure there is no adverse effect on the integrity of the site in accordance with the Conservation of Habitats and Species Regulations 2017 (as amended). 
Natural England must be consulted on any proposals which reach the appropriate assessment stage of HRA.
Please refer to GCSP Biodiversity Supplementary Planning Document pages 52-53 for further information. The Institute of Lighting Professionals GN08 Bats and Artificial Lighting also provides further guidance.
